title: ArXiv Research Activity: 3,667 CS Submissions in August 2026
description: ArXiv reports significant research activity with 3,667 recent Computer Science submissions as of August 20, 2026, and 3,577 entries in the Artificial Intelligence category (cs.AI) for August 2026. On August 21, 2026 alone, there were 222 new submissions. Total arXiv submissions across all categories reached 3,140,535. Submissions typically post Sunday through Thursday with a 2:00 PM Eastern deadline for same-day 8:00 PM publication.
author: ArXiv

title: Andrej Karpathy: End of 'The Era of Typing Computer Code'
description: Andrej Karpathy reports that programming underwent a dramatic transformation in December 2025, marking the end of 'the era of typing computer code into an editor.' Before December, coding agents 'basically didn't work,' but since then models have gained 'significantly higher quality, long-term coherence and tenacity,' completing complex multi-step tasks that previously took entire weekends. Karpathy describes an agent independently setting up SSH keys, installing vLLM, benchmarking models, creating endpoints, building a web UI, testing everything, and generating documentation—all within 30 minutes. The emerging discipline involves 'ascending the layers of abstraction to set up long-running orchestrator' systems managing multiple parallel coding instances.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Warp Factories: Out-of-the-Box Software Factory for AI Development
description: TechCrunch reports on Warp's introduction of 'Warp Factories,' a new infrastructure system designed as an 'out-of-the-box software factory for AI development.' The platform aims to streamline the creation of AI software factories and reduce complexity in AI development, allowing teams to deploy AI coding capabilities without building foundational infrastructure from scratch. This represents a broader trend toward standardized tools for AI development workflows.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI News of the Week: Beyond Demos into Questions of Trust
description: Weekly AI news summary (August 11-18, 2026) highlighting a major industry shift: AI is moving beyond impressive demonstrations into questions of trust, ownership, infrastructure, and profit. Key developments include OpenAI's breakthrough analog AI chip, new workplace AI learning systems reading more like humans, drone training systems with virtual rewards, and machine learning pipelines for artistic recognition. Generative AI has reached 53% population-level adoption in just three years.
author: Industry Analysis

title: Anyone Can Write Code Now, So What Gets You Hired?
description: Super Data Science Podcast Episode 1019 (August 18, 2026) with Priyanka Vergadia. Episode addresses how AI coding assistants have lowered barriers to entry for programming, forcing employers to shift focus toward higher-value competencies that AI cannot easily replicate. Discussion covers differentiating skills beyond pure code generation including problem-solving, system design capabilities, communication and collaboration abilities, understanding business context, adaptability and learning aptitude, and architectural thinking.
author: Super Data Science Podcast with Priyanka Vergadia
